authoredPrompt: This figure presents the mass spectrum of chloroethane as a bar-line plot on a pale beige field. The vertical axis reads "Relative abundance (%)" and runs from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks every 20 units; the horizontal axis, labeled "m/z" and followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, spans 10 to 70 with tick marks every 5 units. Inline text near the top center identifies the sample as "CH3CH2Cl" with "MW = 64.5". Each ion is drawn as a thin vertical line whose height encodes its abundance. The densest group sits between about 25 and 30, where three tall lines rise to just above 90 percent and to roughly 85 and 75 percent, with shorter lines beside them and a small cluster near 35 to 37. A medium line near 49 reaches about 25 percent, with a shorter one near 51. At the far right a line at 64 climbs to the full 100 percent and carries the label "M (64)", while a line at 66 reaching about 30 percent is labeled "M + 2"; several short lines fall between 62 and 65. Setting those two labeled lines side by side lets the reader take their height ratio directly, roughly three to one — the signature of an element present as two isotopes in that natural abundance.
authoredInteractions:
- Click on the M (64) or M + 2 peak to highlight the paired molecular-ion lines, show their relative-height ratio beside the bracket, and make clear how the chlorine isotope pattern produces the roughly 3:1 signature.
- Hover over any fragment line to reveal its m/z and relative abundance while dimming neighboring sticks, making clear that peak position identifies an ion mass and peak height encodes how often that ion appears.
authoredContext:
The fact that some elements have two common isotopes gives their mass spectra a distinctive appearance. Chlorine, for example, exists as two isotopes, 35Cl and 37Cl, in roughly a 3: 1 ratio. In a sample of chloroethane, three out of four molecules contain a 35Cl atom and one out of four has a 37Cl atom. In the mass spectrum of chloroethane (the figure we see the molecular ion (M) at m/z = 64 for ions that contain a 35Cl and another peak at m/z = 66, called the M + 2 peak, for ions containing a 37Cl. The ratio of the relative abundance of M: M + 2 is about 3: 1, a reflection of the isotopic abundances of chlorine.

Mass spectrum of chloroethane.

The mass spectrum of chloroethane with two peaks at m / z 64 and 66, labeled M and M + 2, on a 3 to 1 height ratio.

In the case of bromine, the isotopic distribution is 50.7% 79Br and 49.3% 81Br. In the mass spectrum of 1-bromohexane (the figure) the molecular ion appears at m/z = 164 for 79Br-containing ions and the M + 2 peak is at m/z = 166 for 81Br-containing ions. The ions at m/z = 135 and 137 are informative as well. The two nearly equally large peaks tell us that the ions at those m/z values still contain the bromine atom. The peak at m/z = 85, on the other hand, does not contain bromine because there is not a large peak at m/z = 87.
